answer: Keep your car insured until the sale is complete and the car is in our hands, then cancel the policy or remove the car only after you sign the paperwork, and ask your insurer about a refund for the unused premium. If your car has North Carolina plates, leave them on the car, because plate rules follow the state that issued the plates, not where you live (for example, Virginia, Georgia and Texas plates are removed and kept, and California plates go back to California within 10 days with form NW-PLT-1). Before handing the car over, remove toll tags and parking stickers, clear garage door codes, unpair your phone, and remove the car from any connected-car app account. If the car is registered in another state, it also needs an emissions certificate from a North Carolina inspection station before a North Carolina store can buy it.
